question: Should OpenClaw accept the RFC’s model where an explicitly consented Claw package may create instruction-bearing files in a new agent workspace and record ownership in shared persistent state?
rationale: Code review can assess confinement and persistence mechanics, but only maintainers can authorize the new package trust boundary and permanent Claw lifecycle model.

options.title: Pause for RFC acceptance
options.body: Keep this stacked PR open but unmergeable until the parent RFC explicitly approves the workspace-content and ownership model.

options.title: Approve with complete proof
options.body: Accept the direction and require redacted fresh-install, upgrade, created-file, and claw_workspace_files row evidence on the final stack before merge.

options.title: Narrow the lifecycle
options.body: Limit the first accepted Claw release to non-instruction metadata until maintainers define a stricter policy for package-supplied workspace content.

recommendation.title: Pause for RFC acceptance
recommendation.body: Keep this stacked PR open but unmergeable until the parent RFC explicitly approves the workspace-content and ownership model.

likelyOwner.reason: The decision spans core product direction, shared persistent state, and filesystem trust boundaries associated with this history.
